What it means: The Select Board conducted routine municipal business and reviewed upcoming Town Meeting warrant articles [15:21], [2:01:30]. During the session, the board issued proclamations recognizing LGBTQIA+ History Month [28:47] and White Cane Day [31:23], approved the promotion of Lieutenant Hayes to Deputy Superintendent [49:09], [52:10], and voted on appointments to the Youth Council [45:33] and the Transportation Board [1:12:28]. The board also authorized a Memorandum of Agreement for 26 Pleasant Street concerning public mitigation measures and site commitments [1:15:41], [1:23:51], [1:52:36], and endorsed warrant articles regarding housing trust funding policies [2:38:37], [2:57:53], school zone safety initiatives [2:59:24], [2:59:43], and outdoor lighting standards [3:00:14], [3:18:21].

Who moved it: Motions were put forward by members of the Select Board throughout the meeting, with votes taken by members Bernard, Amanda, Michael, and Anthony [45:45], [45:47], [52:30], [52:33], [1:12:58], [1:13:03], [2:01:12], [2:01:16], [2:58:28], [2:58:31], [2:59:48], [3:18:29], [3:18:32]. Specifically, motions were made to confirm appointments to the Youth Council [45:33], approve the police promotion recommended by Chief Pastor [49:09], [52:10], appoint Gregory Wheeler to the Transportation Board [1:12:28], approve the 26 Pleasant Street Memorandum of Agreement [1:52:36], and recommend favorable action on Warrant Articles 17 [2:57:53], 11 [2:59:43], 12, and 13 [3:18:21].

What to watch: The warrant articles reviewed during the meeting will proceed to Town Meeting for final evaluation and consideration [1:18:45], [2:00:53]. Development plans for 26 Pleasant Street remain subject to subsequent special permit decisions through the Zoning Board of Appeals, further design review [1:23:39], [1:44:54], and upcoming financial impact reports [1:59:36]. In addition, the board deferred action on proposed updates to the town's fraudulent conduct policy to allow board members time to review the proposed language before taking a final vote [3:18:50], [3:24:20].

summary: The board received community updates [15:37] and approved prior meeting minutes [26:44] before issuing proclamations recognizing National Coming Out Day [28:06], Disability Employment Awareness Month, and White Cane Safety Day [29:33]. Discussions were held regarding a dredging excavation contract bid [20:03], appointments to town advisory committees [32:25], town administrator terms [41:21], and the promotion of Derek Hayes to police deputy superintendent [49:10], as well as the appointment of Gregory Wheeler to the Transportation Board [1:12:38]. Members reviewed several upcoming warrant articles, including Article 16 regarding a community benefits memorandum of agreement [1:15:41], Article 19 on indigenous representation [2:03:28], Article 20 supporting Vision Zero traffic enforcement [2:13:26], Article 3 concerning transportation network revenue allocations [2:33:45], Article 17 regarding Community Preservation Act funding for the Housing Trust [2:39:51], and Articles 12 and 13 addressing outdoor lighting regulations [2:59:55]. Finally, the board discussed proposed revisions to the policy on fraudulent conduct [3:18:50].
